memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses said to the people, 'Commemorate this day, the day you came out of
Egypt, out of the land of slavery, because the LORD brought you out of it with a
mighty hand. Eat nothing containing yeast.'" - Ex 13:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses tells them to remember, and he tells them exactly what to remember: not
their courage, not their escape, but that "the LORD brought you out."

That phrase does a lot of work. Israel did nothing that night except put blood on
a doorframe and stay indoors. They did not fight, negotiate, or outwit anyone.
The mighty hand was God's.

We are wired to forget this. Give us a few years of freedom and we start telling
the story with ourselves at the centre. We remember our decision, our discipline,
our turning point. All of that may be real, but it is not the mighty hand.

Notice also the phrase "the land of slavery." Moses names it honestly. He does
not let them romanticise where they came from. That matters, because within a
few chapters they will start doing exactly that.

Healthy remembering holds two things together: the honest truth about where we
were, and the clear truth about who got us out. Paul does this constantly. "Such
were some of you. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified"
(1 Cor 6:11).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you tell your story, who is at the centre of it?
2. Are you honest about what God rescued you from?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You brought me out with a mighty hand. Keep me from taking credit for
what only You could do. Amen.
